To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the formation of descending motor pathways to the spinal motor neurons follows a specific sequence, (ii) the sequence of development of the descending pathways is paralleled by changes in locomotor pattern, and (iii) the development of descending motor pathways in anurans is not only a good model for mammalian development but may also be used as an experimental model for developmental neurobiology.
'the developmental sequence in the ingrowth of descending brain stem pathways in anuran amphibians parallels the changes in the locomotor pattern during development'.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental mechanisms involved in the establishment of neuronal connections in the developing brain stem-spinal system in anurans.
the development of motor systems in anurans.
the development of descending pathways in anurans, and the relation with locomotor pattern.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anuran development is a good model to study the development and organization of descending systems.
the development of motor systems in anurans and mammals are similar.
the development of descending pathways in anurans is a complex process that is still far from being completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of motor systems in anurans is a complex and protracted process.
the development of descending brainstem systems in the anuran is a highly regulated process.
the formation of descending brainstem pathways to the spinal motor system is a highly conserved phenomenon in vertebrates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmental sequence of motor system formation in anurans is remarkably similar to that of mammals.
the development of descending motor systems in anurans is a complex and protracted process that parallels the development of locomotor pattern.
anurans offer an excellent opportunity to study the developmental aspects of neuronal connections in the context of the evolution of the vertebrate brain.
